public_rationale: The ordinary comparable-capability reading is supported. DeepSeek documented improved efficiency and sharply lower prices while retaining comparable benchmark performance during the claimed period. Broader research corroborates the direction of price-performance and efficiency gains. Peer-reviewed research in April 2026 explicitly finds that hallucinations still persist. This does not establish that the newest frontier models or complete agent tasks always become cheaper.
limitations: The concrete within-period efficiency comparison is vendor-reported.
The broad independent cost study also includes months before January 2025 and is context only.
Falling unit or capability-adjusted costs can coexist with rising total inference spending.

our_interpretation: Assess the retrospective trend from the January 2025 prediction through July 20, 2026.
The ordinary reading is declining resources and price for comparable useful capability, alongside continuing factual errors and unreliable outputs.
This does not require every model, the latest flagship, or total customer spending to become cheaper.
Efficiency and price are separate propositions; a price cut alone does not prove computational efficiency.
criteria.support_condition: Within-period evidence documents lower prices and improved computational efficiency at broadly comparable capability, while contemporary research documents continuing hallucinations or reliability failures.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Representative evidence rejects the comparable-capability cost and efficiency trend, or establishes that hallucinations and reliability failures no longer persist.

evidence.explanation: DeepSeek reports improved long-context efficiency, benchmark parity with V3.1-Terminus and an immediate API price reduction exceeding 50%. This is a concrete within-period example supporting both efficiency and price, although the performance comparison is vendor-reported.
The paper identifies continuing confident falsehoods and their consequences for reliability. It directly supports persistence, without implying that error rates never improve.

The April 2024–November 2025 dataset finds substantial price reductions at fixed benchmark capability and algorithmic efficiency gains. It also finds increasing costs for running the advancing frontier, so it supports the interpretation while materially qualifying an unadjusted-price reading.
